ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle B=90^\circ$, $AB=4$, $BC>AB$, and point $D$ is on side $BC$. Among all the parallelograms $ADCE$ with $AC$ as the diagonal, what is the minimum value of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: The intersection point of the diagonals of parallelogram ADCE is the midpoint O of AC. When $OD \perp BC$, OD is minimal, which means DE is minimal.\\
Since $AB \perp BC$,\\
Therefore, $OD \parallel AB$,\\
Therefore, at this time, OD is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
Therefore, $OD = \frac{1}{2}AB = 2$,\\
Since parallelogram ADCE is a parallelogram,\\
Therefore, $DE = 2OD = \boxed{4}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, B is at the lower left and is marked with a right angle, BC is the left vertical side, and BA is the bottom horizontal side; A is at the lower right, and C is at the upper left. D is located on BC, E is at the upper right, and quadrilateral ADCE is drawn as a parallelogram, with the two diagonals AC and DE intersecting at point O. Reasoning: Let O be the intersection point of the diagonals AC and DE of parallelogram ADCE. Because the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, O is the midpoint of AC, and at the same time O is also the midpoint of DE, so DE=2OD. When D moves on BC, O is a fixed point, so to make DE minimal, it is only necessary to make OD minimal. The shortest distance from the fixed point O to the line BC is the perpendicular segment, so take OD⊥BC. Also because in the problem ∠B=90°, that is, AB⊥BC, at this time OD∥AB. In triangle ABC, O is the midpoint of AC; draw OD∥AB through O to intersect BC at D, then D is the midpoint of BC, and OD is the midline of triangle ABC. Therefore OD=AB/2=4/2=2. Thus the minimum DE=2OD=4.
